facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized on 22.1.2012. Two children were born out of the wedlock. The respondent is a Muslim by religion. Petitioner seeks declaration that marriage is null and void with consequential prayer for permanent prohibitory injunction.

legal_principles.principle: At the preliminary stage, the Court is not called upon to record a finding about truth or otherwise of the allegations made in the plaint.
legal_principles.held: The only question relevant for consideration at such a stage is whether on the basis of the averments made in the plaint and the prayers contained therein, the suit is a suit for annulment of marriage within the meaning of the Hindu Marriage Act or for a declaration under the Specific Relief Act.

legal_principles.principle: A plaint filed in the case at hand is not a petition under the Hindu Marriage Act and/or Special Marriage Act if it does not ask for annulment on grounds specified in Sections 11 and 12.
legal_principles.held: From the aforementioned, it is evident that the plaint filed in the case at hand is not a petition under the Hindu Marriage Act and/or Special Marriage Act. On the face of the plaint, it really appears to be a suit for declaration as to the status of the parties.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: advising on the maintainability of a civil suit
guiding clients on the specific remedies available under Hindu Marriage Act
